class: entry whose every ground is a distinction

expect.why: a `distinguishes` act says what the entry is not; an entry all of whose grounds are distinctions has stated a difference and rested on nothing, and the Warrant has nothing to argue from

note: K26 is the near-negative: the same distinction beside a real ground, which every checker must leave alone. The pair is what keeps the rule from being satisfied by a checker that rejects the act itself. `references` says nothing here, and that is deliberate — a distinction is legal against a target of any status, because it is a claim about two Scopes rather than about a truth.
